title: Protein succinylation shows a negative pattern in regulating lamb tenderization
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

The effects of some common protein post-translational modifications (PTMs) such as phosphorylation, acetylation, and S-nitrosylation have been widely shown to influence meat quality development. An increasing number of new PTMs have been discovered that are involved in life activities. Importantly, it is reported that protein succinylation impacts numerous energy metabolic pathways. Based on the important role of energy metabolism in postmortem meat, we hypothesized that protein succinylation regulates meat quality.

RESULTS

The objective of this study was to explore the role of protein succinylation in meat tenderization. The longissimus thoracis muscles of small-tailed Han lambs with differential tenderness were selected according to shear force measured at 0.5 h and 5 days postmortem. Succinylome analysis was performed to uncover the pathways associated with protein succinylation under pre-rigor and post-rigor conditions. Succinylome analysis displayed a negative regulatory pattern between protein succinylation and meat tenderness. Differentially succinylated proteins were enriched in pathways such as glycolysis, muscle contraction, the tricarboxylic acid cycle and oxidative phosphorylation. The results of pairwise associations showed significantly positive correlations between 22 individual succinylated proteins and meat shear force. In addition, actin and desmin exhibited a more stable structure following succinylation.

CONCLUSION

The present study provides a comprehensive succinylome profile of postmortem meat tenderness development, which is useful for further studies on the mechanistic regulation of meat quality. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
